title: Signal Desktop conversations (Flatpak)
whyItMatters: The Flatpak build keeps the same Signal conversation database and attachments inside its sandbox folder, so a native-only check will miss it.
source: Flatpak sandbox permissions: per-app config lives in ~/.var/app/<app-id>/config; Signal's Flathub id is org.signal.Signal: https://docs.flatpak.org/en/latest/sandbox-permissions.html
notes: Same sql/db.sqlite, attachments and logs as the native install, relocated into the sandbox. The database key stays in the desktop keyring.

cleanup.exportFirst: Save any photos or files you want to keep from the conversations: Signal keeps no copy of them on a server.
cleanup.signOut: On your phone, open Signal > Settings > Linked devices and unlink this computer, so the account no longer trusts it.
steps: In Signal Desktop, open Settings and choose Delete Data to clear the local message store.
Quit Signal Desktop from its tray icon.
Uninstall the Signal Flatpak from the App Center or from your Flatpak tool.
Move the folder named in the plan to the Trash and empty the Trash.
cleanup.risk: Removes the local copy of every conversation, attachment and draft inside the sandbox. The messages stay on the linked phone only.
